details: CONFIRMED. closed_on(main, base, tip, slug) reads only `<base>:.relay/queue/<slug>.json`. Before this branch lands, every closed
item at the base is at `.relay/queue/done/<slug>.json`, so `before` is None and `_closed_at(None)` is False: every closed item at
the tip counts as closed by the branch. step_queue then calls check_refusal for each, and the branch holds a check of none of
them. The design (6.2) wrote "absent or has no closed_at"; it did not see that the move itself makes 69 items "absent at base".
The gate is green because no test merges a branch whose range contains the move. Size: 15 agent minutes.
evidence: python3 -I: closed_on over the 69 closed fix items at HEAD vs merge_base(master, HEAD) -> "69 closed_on calls 0.83 s; true: 69"
Refused queue item a-bench-with-set-leaves-the-main-checkout-dirty is closed without a test or a check: no check of this fix: run delegate:checker on the branch's head, then close '...'
held_fix_items('.', riders=True) -> all 69 closed fix items listed as held by this branch.
failing_case: Merge of wt/drop-done itself, judged by the branch's own hook: step_queue('/Users/amidman/relay', 'master', 'wt/drop-done').
At the merge base the file .relay/queue/a-bench-with-set-leaves-the-main-checkout-dirty.json is absent (it lives under done/ on
master); at the tip it is present with closed_at. closed_on returns True ("absent at base" counts as not closed), for all 69
closed fix items. Now: Refused "queue item a-bench-with-set-leaves-the-main-checkout-dirty is closed without a test or a check:
no check of this fix ...". Should: allowed (the move closes nothing). The same holds for any branch that took master after a
close landed with the old code and then ran relay queue migrate (design 6.1's re-run path), and for the train's closing_tip.
fix_hint: In closed_on, read base at both paths: `<base>:.relay/queue/<slug>.json` and `<base>:.relay/queue/done/<slug>.json` (one cat_batch
of three blobs); closed at base in either place means not closed on the branch. Add a temp-repo test for pass case 1 (hook and
held_fix_items) and confirm it fails with the done/ read removed.
pass_cases: 1. Temp repo: master has .relay/queue/done/x.json (fix, closed_at set); branch only does git mv done/x.json -> x.json. step_queue(master, branch) does not refuse; closed_on(main, merge_base, branch, "x") is False.
2. Branch sets closed_at in place on open fix x with no test: refused "closed without a test or a check" (today's T15n, must keep).
3. Branch adds a new fix item y already closed (absent at base, closed at tip) with no test: refused, as today a file added under done/ was.
4. held_fix_items(worktree, riders=True) on the move branch returns no item the move only renamed.
reason: tests/test_queue_in_place.py:220 and :250 pass, fail at 000c8cf; :230 and :241 pass-cases pass. lib/relay_queue.py closed_on reads done/ at base.
findings.summary: closed_on counts every item the move brought out of done/ as closed on this branch, so the new merge hook refuses this very branch (69 fix items need a test and a check)

details: CONFIRMED. The hook in force at a merge is the default branch's (the plugins load from the main checkout), but record_rules runs the
branch's lib: the parse signature is a contract between two versions, and the change broke it in one step. Only this change's own
merge (and any train holding it) hits it; after it lands the new hook passes 2 rows, which old libs accept. Size: 10 agent minutes.
evidence: -> TypeError: parse() takes 2 positional arguments but 3 were given
failing_case: The hook that guards the merge is loaded from the main checkout (/Users/amidman/relay, on master; settings.json marketplace path).
Its record_rules runs the branch's lib/relay_queue.py with RULES_RUNNER `relay_queue.parse(slug, text, where) for slug, text, where
in rows`. The branch's parse is now parse(slug, text). Now: TypeError "parse() takes 2 positional arguments but 3 were given", the
runner exits non-zero, record_rules raises, the merge is refused. Should: master's hook judges the branch's items and lets the
merge on (or refuses only for a real reason).
fix_hint: Keep `where=None` as an accepted, ignored third parameter of parse (and check/serialize if any old caller passes it), with a
docstring line saying it stays for the default branch's hook until the next change; a test that runs master's runner string
pass_cases: 1. master's RULES_RUNNER fed [["x", "<well-formed open item>", "open"]] with the branch's lib/ prints [{...,"problems": []}] (no TypeError).
2. The same with "done" as the third element for a closed item: parses with no folder problem (the folder rule is gone).
3. The branch's own RULES_RUNNER with 2-element rows keeps working (parse(slug, text)).
4. A lib of an older branch (parse(slug, text, where=None)) judged by the new hook with 2-element rows keeps working.
reason: tests/test_queue_in_place.py:278 passes, fails at 000c8cf (TypeError); :284 pass-case passes. parse keeps where=None.
findings.summary: master's live merge hook passes (slug, text, where) to the branch's parse, which no longer takes `where`: the record-rules process dies and the merge of this change is refused

details: CONFIRMED by measurement. Project rule, principle 2 (Waste): waste that repeats on every run is MEDIUM. A file the range did not
change cannot have been closed on the branch (its blob is the same at base and tip), so the call is always False for those items
once F1 is fixed. Size: 10 agent minutes.
evidence: python3 -I: 69 closed_on calls over the closed fix items at HEAD -> 0.83 s
merge.py 186-193: loop over every path at the tip; the closed_on call is reached for every meta with kind fix and state done
failing_case: Any merge of a branch that changed no queue item, in this repo after the change: step_queue iterates the 69 closed fix items at
the tip and calls relay_queue.closed_on for each (one cat-file --batch process each). Now: 69 git processes, about 0.83 s per hook
run, and one more per future close. Should: closed_on only for the item files the range changed (changed_files), as design 6.2
says ("one cat-file --batch for every item the range changed"); a branch that changed no item spends no closed_on call.
fix_hint: Before closed_on, `if path not in changed: continue` where changed = set(changed_files.split("\0")); or batch the base and tip
blobs of the changed items in one cat_batch.
pass_cases: 1. A branch that changes only lib/a.py over a queue with N closed fix items: step_queue makes 0 closed_on calls (count with a patched closed_on).
2. A branch that closes fix x in place without a test: still refused "closed without a test or a check" (T15n).
3. A branch that took master after master closed x (x in the tip, not in the range): x is not judged, allowed (T15n3 last case).
reason: tests/test_queue_in_place.py:257 passes, fails at 000c8cf; merge.py skips paths not in changed.
findings.summary: principle 2: step_queue runs closed_on (one git process) for every closed fix item at the tip, not only the items the range changed: 69 processes, 0.83 s on every merge check, growing with the queue
